title: `AppTest` fails to resolve imports when using a src layout
body: When using the [src layout](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/discussions/src-layout-vs-flat-layout/), `AppTest.from_file()` fails to resolve internal module imports, even when the tests are run from the project root. Is this a bug or is there a specific syntax/configuration I should use to let AppTest know it should look into the src directory?

comments.body:
**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-13909)

This is a bug in how `AppTest` (and the underlying `ScriptRunner`) sets up `sys.path` when executing scripts. The root cause is in `modified_sys_path` (`lib/streamlit/runtime/scriptrunner/exec_code.py`), which is intended to prepend the script's **directory** to `sys.path` during execution. However, it receives and inserts the full **file path** (e.g., `/project/src/myapp/app.py`) instead of the parent directory (`/project/src/myapp/`). Since Python expects directories in `sys.path`, this has no effect on import resolution. In a flat layout, this bug is masked because the CWD (already in `sys.path`) typically matches the script's directory. In a src layout, the script lives in a subdirectory (e.g., `src/myapp/`) that is not the CWD, so sibling module imports fail with `ModuleNotFoundError`.

The fix would involve changing `modified_sys_path` to use `os.path.dirname(main_script_path)` instead of the raw file path, or having `AppTest` explicitly add the script's parent directory to `sys.path`.

### Related Issues

- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8154 — `AppTest` doesn't work with relative filenames in `st.sidebar.page_link()`. Related because it also involves path resolution issues within the `AppTest` framework.
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8429 — Unable to test a multipage app with custom sidebar using `AppTest`. Related because the test runner cannot resolve page paths correctly, which is another manifestation of path handling issues in `AppTest`.
